description: the seal becomes an unkeyed sha-256 over the same terms: anyone who can read the row can recompute it (H4 C11:2615-2623). It is also a second hashing scheme under src/widgets, so the H6 ratchet must see it too.

description: one H4 term leaves the pre-image: `principal_proof_hash`, so a token minted for one principal seals the same as one minted for another.
the stored seal is compared with `===`: same verdicts, measurable latency (§3, indistinguishable latency).
a missing term verifies: the verifier answers `ok` when a column the seal covers is null or empty, so an erased or half-written row passes Gate 1.

the key-version guard admits every version, so a seal minted under a rotated key would be verified under the current one (AREA-C: the interim verifies under the single current version and refuses otherwise).

the H6 ratchet's scanner is neutralised, so it would report no hashing site anywhere and pass over a widget layer that had grown a second scheme. A ratchet that cannot see is the failure mode a ratchet is most likely to have.
